newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - May 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - May 21.

text.p: Aussies cry foul over fire blight: New Zealand is defending itself against media accusations of sabotage after a new discovery by a New Zealand scientist of fire blight in an Australian state. Page 1.

Dole-work legality questioned: The government's planned work-for-the-dole scheme might breach international conventions on forced labour, Labour employment spokesman Steve Maharey said on Tuesday. Page 2.

Compulsory super gets thumbs down in survey: Most people would vote against superannuation if the referendum scheduled for September were held now, according to a survey conducted for Colonial New Zealand. Page 19.

Sovereign listing on agenda: Stock analysts said the time was right for Sovereign to gloat after the spectacular success of Colonial Group's float on the New Zealand and Australian stock exchanges on Monday. Page 19.

Casino unlikely on Wakefield site: A five-level office block remains the most likely option for a large Courtney Place site in Wellington, despite reports that an agreement has been signed to put a casino on the land. Page 19.

Foreign deal for cabinet eye only: The cabinet is preparing to sign an international agreement liberalising foreign investment rules without seeing the need to consult the New Zealand First or National caucuses or debate the issue in Parliament.
Bondholders finally learn facts: Skellerup Group bondholders have been given details by their trustee of substantial changes to the company's banking covenants.

Secure Internet deals soon says Visa: Secure credit card transactions on the Internet will be available next year, the Tokyo-based head of Visa International (Asia-Pacific), Dennis Goggin, said on Tuesday.
Doubts cast on cable TV market: A bleak lookout is predicted for one of the two cable television companies currently investing heavily in setting up networks.

Prebble battles 'palace': Wellington Central MP Richard Prebble on Tuesday vowed to force a vote in Parliament on the planned ministerial services building -- saying that the proposal was economic, social and political folly. Page 2.
Southpower hums with Enerco: Southpower has lifted its bottom-line profit almost one-third to $25.18 million, with a kick along from its North Island gas subsidiary, Enerco New Zealand. Page 26.
BOP Electricity lifts profit: Bay of Plenty Electricity will be able to generate all its electricity needs by the end of the year. Page 27.
